name: United Airlines Holdings
description: United flies passengers and cargo through hubs in the US and across the Atlantic, Pacific and Latin America, with regional flying done by partner carriers under capacity purchase agreements (6.1 percent of 2025 capacity). Ticket sales were 90.5 percent of 2025 revenue; the rest is cargo and 'other', which includes MileagePlus loyalty revenue from credit card issuers (Chase), partners and the programme. It reports a single segment. 2025 operating income was $4.7B (8 percent margin) on revenue of $59.1B; in the June 2026 quarter revenue jumped 16 percent but fuel cost rose 84 percent, so operating income fell to $1.1B from $1.3B.

gics.note: Conventional filing: GICS sector and 'Passenger Airlines' sub-industry as listed on Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (read 2026-10-01); the list does not show the industry group or industry. SEC SIC code 4512 (Air Transportation, Scheduled) per EDGAR.

hq.note: Chicago, IL per EDGAR business address and Wikipedia S&P 500 list

employees.note: About 113,200 employees, about 83 percent represented by US labor organisations. FY2025 10-K

businessLines.name: Passenger
businessLines.how: Travelers pay per ticket at booking; revenue is capacity (seats flown) times load factor times yield, with premium cabins and international routes earning more per seat. Regional partners fly under capacity purchase agreements, so United books the ticket revenue and pays the partner a fee ($2,693M in 2025).
businessLines.description: Mainline and United Express regional ticket sales, domestic and international (Atlantic, Pacific, Latin America).

revenue.note: FY2024 $51,829M (+3.1 percent) on capacity +6.1 percent and passengers +4.3 percent; PRASM 16.18 cents vs 16.66. H1 2026 $29,267M vs $25,696M; Q2 2026 $16,100M vs $13,836M.

businessLines.revenueNote: FY2024 $51,829M (+3.1 percent) on capacity +6.1 percent and passengers +4.3 percent; PRASM 16.18 cents vs 16.66. H1 2026 $29,267M vs $25,696M; Q2 2026 $16,100M vs $13,836M.

businessLines.name: Loyalty (MileagePlus) and other operating revenue
businessLines.how: Chase and non-airline partners (card issuers, hotels, car rental, retail) pay United for miles awarded to their customers, which United recognises partly as marketing revenue and partly deferred until miles are redeemed for flights; Chase agreement also covers marketing access to United's customer database.
businessLines.description: MileagePlus miles sold to the Chase co-brand credit card and other partners, plus other revenue such as lounges and services; reported in 'Other operating revenue'.

revenue.note: Total 'Other operating revenue' (+10.4 percent from $3,491M), up mainly on mileage revenue from non-airline partners including credit-card spending. The loyalty portion alone was not separately extracted.

businessLines.revenueNote: Total 'Other operating revenue' (+10.4 percent from $3,491M), up mainly on mileage revenue from non-airline partners including credit-card spending. The loyalty portion alone was not separately extracted.

businessLines.name: Cargo
businessLines.how: Shippers pay per kilogram or shipment; capacity is a by-product of passenger flights.
businessLines.description: Freight carried in the bellies of scheduled passenger flights plus interline, charter and ground trucking.

revenue.note: FY2024 $1,743M (+2.1 percent); cargo revenue ton miles 3,626M vs 3,604M

brands.name: United Airlines and United Express (regional partners)
brands.share: Regional is about 6.1 percent of total 2025 capacity; regional capacity purchase cost $2,693M (+7.0 percent)

brands.name: MileagePlus
brands.share: Co-brand credit card with JPMorgan Chase; members redeemed miles for about 4.3 million non-flight awards in 2025 (club memberships, car, hotel, merchandise)
